item.research_question: Can FeCoNiAlTi high-entropy alloy (HEA) serve as an effective reinforcement to improve the microstructure and hardness of 316L stainless steel when fabricated via Selective Laser Melting (SLM), and what is the optimal reinforcement ratio?
item.material_system: 316L stainless steel matrix reinforced with FeCoNiAlTi high-entropy alloy (HEA) at 2 wt.%, 5 wt.%, and 10 wt.%
item.processing_route: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) using an HBD-100 device with a single mode fiber laser (180 W power, 60 μm spot diameter, 30 μm layer thickness, 50 μm hatch distance) at scanning speeds of 650, 800, and 1000 mm/s under argon atmosphere; powders (15–53 μm) mixed for 2 h at 45 r/min.
item.test_conditions: Nanoindentation performed with a Hysitron TI980 at a maximum load of 5 mN, loading rate of 1 mN/s, holding time of 2 s; EBSD analysis at 20 kV with 0.4 μm step size; optical microscopy for porosity; samples etched in 25 mL HNO3 and 75 mL HCL for 10 s.
key_findings: The composite with 2 wt.% HEA reinforcement achieved the maximum relative density of 99.3% at a scanning speed of 650 mm/s.
Pure 316L stainless steel exhibited columnar grains with an average size of 15.86 μm, while the 2 wt.% HEA composite showed equiaxed grains with a drastically reduced size of 0.66 μm.
The percentage of low angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) in the 2 wt.% HEA composite was significantly higher than in the pure 316L stainless steel matrix.
The nanohardness of the 2 wt.% HEA-reinforced composite (5.70–5.86 GPa) was approximately twice that of the pure 316L stainless steel (2.49–2.63 GPa).
Increasing the scanning speed from 650 to 1000 mm/s increased porosity and caused cracks to grow from 15 to 183 μm due to reduced laser power density and gas entrapment.
HEA reinforcement particles promoted heterogeneous nucleation and a pinning effect, leading to grain refinement from the cellular structure typical of SLM to finer equiaxed grains.
item.mechanism: The addition of HEA reinforcement particles promotes heterogeneous nucleation and exerts a pinning effect, which transforms the microstructure from columnar to equiaxed and refines the grain size to the nanoscale (0.66 μm). This grain refinement, combined with a higher volume fraction of low angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) that hinder dislocation movement, is the primary reason for the significant increase in hardness.
item.limitations: The study notes that the existence of pores in SLM samples deteriorates mechanical and chemical properties, and that increasing reinforcement ratio or scanning speed leads to higher porosity and metallurgical defects like cracks.
item.future_work: The authors state that the specific strengthening mechanism and the effect of microstructure on hardness need to be studied further, and that additional tests such as tensile, wear, and corrosion should be carried out.
quotes: The nanohardness of the composite reinforced with 2 wt.% FeCoNiAlTi HEA is twice as high as the 316L stainless steel matrix.
The grain size decreases drastically, and the percentage of the low angle grain boundary in the composite is much higher than in the 316L stainless steel matrix.
In the future, the specific strengthening mechanism and the effect of microstructure on hardness need to be studied.
